findingDetails.title: Shared Git common-directory trust admits branch-controlled hook code
findingDetails.case: A maintainer checks out an untrusted contributor branch in a linked worktree of a trusted clone and commits. The trust check sees the same Git common directory, leaves SOURCE_ROOT pointed at the checked-out tree, then sources that tree’s hook-flags.sh during the commit.
findingDetails.evidence: The gate treats equal common Git directories as trusted and only marks a repository untrusted when the common directories differ or the local opt-in is absent. It then sources hook-flags.sh from SOURCE_ROOT, which was selected from the current repository tree. A branch that changes that sourced file can execute shell code as the committing user.
findingDetails.userImpact: A contributor-controlled branch can run arbitrary commands with the maintainer’s local permissions when the maintainer commits from a linked worktree.
findingDetails.scopeProof: This claim is limited to the scoped pre-commit trust gate and its immediate source operation at lines 43-61. No cross-consumer claim is made.
findingDetails.recommendation: Bind trust to an immutable hook source or revision, or require an explicit local opt-in for branch-controlled worktree hook code. Add a scoped case for an untrusted linked-worktree branch.
findingDetails.claim: The common-directory equality check is insufficient to establish that the hook scripts in the checked-out worktree are trusted, allowing branch-controlled shell code to execute at commit time.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: The check rejects a separate clone unless its local skilled.trustRepoHooks setting is true. In the selected hook code, I looked for a revision or branch-origin check and an immutable source for hook-flags.sh; neither appears in the trust-to-source path.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The intended trust model may treat every branch and linked worktree under a trusted Git common directory as trusted by the operator. Under that policy, the code is consistent with repository-level trust, though the security boundary is broader than branch-level trust.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the security contract explicitly accepts all branches and linked worktrees sharing a trusted common directory, and maintainers cannot be induced to commit from contributor-controlled branches without ordinary code review.

searchLedger.invariant: Only code whose trust has been established should be sourced by a commit hook.

searchActions.result: Equal common Git directories pass the trust gate, after which hook-flags.sh is sourced from the current repository tree.

searchLedger.rationale: The trust predicate authenticates repository identity but does not authenticate the checked-out branch content.

searchLedger.hypothesis: An arbitrary --hub value could reach a dynamic module path.

searchActions.result: The engine rejects hub IDs absent from HUB_CHILD before constructing and requiring the child paths.

searchLedger.rationale: The dynamic module path is selected only after a fixed hub allowlist lookup.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The inspected loader rejects unknown hub IDs before path construction or require.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A caller-controlled probe prompt could be interpolated into a shell command.

searchActions.result: The child process receives a fixed executable and argv array; the prompt is one argv value and no shell is invoked.

searchLedger.rationale: The user prompt does not enter a shell command string in the execution path.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: spawnSync is called with an argv array and no shell option.

searchLedger.invariant: Untrusted payload data should travel as data, and only required environment keys should cross the bridge.

searchActions.result: The bridge uses a fixed Node argv, JSON on stdin, an explicit environment allowlist, and a timeout.

searchLedger.rationale: The selected bridge path does not interpolate payload text into a shell command or inherit the full environment.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The inspected call passes serialized input via stdin and filters environment keys through NATIVE_BRIDGE_ENV_ALLOWLIST.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Commit-Id contract validation may trust untrusted message or repository metadata.

searchActions.result: The shell tokenizer was inspected, but the Commit-Id policy helper is not listed in the review scope and the full validator-consumer flow was not audited.

searchLedger.rationale: The scoped message parser is only one part of the feature flow.
searchLedger.deferredReason: The Commit-Id helper is outside the explicit scope manifest, so this pass cannot establish end-to-end validation behavior.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Fast Mode configuration may admit unsafe tool or context boundaries.

searchActions.result: The implementation path is present in the workspace but absent from the declared review scope.

searchLedger.rationale: The review target is frozen to the supplied scope file list.
searchLedger.deferredReason: The Pi Fast Mode implementation is outside the supplied review scope and was not inspected.
